THIS WP IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO DECLARE THAT ACQUISITION PROCEEDINGS IN RESPECT OF THE PETITION PROPERTY PURSUANT TO PRELIMINARY NOTIFICATION DATED 21.05.2008 ISSUED U/S 17(1) AND (3) OF THE BDA ACT, 1976 AND THE FINAL NOTIFICATION DATED 18.02.2010 ISSUED U/S 19(1) OF THE BDA ACT, COPIES OF WHICH ARE PRODUCED AT ANNEXURES - C AND D ARE DEEMED TO HAVE BEEN LAPSED IN TERMS OF SECTION 27 OF BDA ACT AND ETC.,
 THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
i) Declare that acquisition proceedings in respect of the petition property pursuant to preliminary Notification No.BDA/COMMR/DC(LA)/ALAO/158/2008-09, Bangalore dated 21.05.200 issued u/s 17(1) and(3) of the BDA Act, 1976 and the Final NC:
2023:KHC:41200 Notification No.UDD51 MNX 2010, Bangalore dated 18.02.2010 issued u/s 19(1) of the BDA Act, copies of which are produced at Annexures-C and D,
are deemed to have been lapsed in terms of Section 27 of BDA Act so far as petition land Sy.No.185/2 of Bhimanakuppe village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk is concerned.
ii) Grant such other order or direction as deems fit to grant in the facts and circumstances of the case.
2.

Sri Girish T.R, learned counsel appearing for Sri Nagaraj R.Nagarbhavi, learned counsel appearing for petitioners submitted that petitioners were absolute owners of 18 guntas of land in Sy.No.185/2 of Bhimanakuppe Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.

It was submitted that said land was sought to be acquired by respondent no.2-BDA under preliminary notification dated 21.05.2008 for formation of Nada Prabhu Kempegowda Layout and final notification was issued on 18.02.2010.
Thereafter respondents did not pursue acquisition and possession was not taken nor scheme implemented.

Therefore, petitioners have sought for declaration that acquisition proceedings are deemed to NC: 2023:KHC:41200 have been lapsed in view of Section 27 of Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 ('BDA Act').
3.

In reply, Sri K.Krishna, learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 referring to statement of objections filed would submit that acquisition proceedings had proceeded with due participation of petitioners and they were also issued notice under Sections 9 and 10 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 on 20.09.2010.
In response, petitioners submitted reply through petitioner no.5 claiming cash compensation.

Subsequently, on 03.11.2011 petitioners executed indemnity bond and agreement Sri Nagamangalaiah vs The State Of Karnataka on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36598135/
4 (Annexure - R1) agreeing to receive compensation towards their respective shares.

sentences.text: Thereafter respondent no.3 passed award (Annexure - R2) which received approval on 22.02.2012.

It was submitted that thereafter petitioners were issued notices under Section 12 of Land Acquisition Act on 08.03.2012 and possession of land was taken on 09.03.2012 by drawing a mahazar signed by petitioners.
NC: 2023:KHC:41200 4.
On examination of records insofar as land in question, it was noted that said land was Inam land and relevant records regarding re-grant had not been produced.
Consequently, compensation assessed was kept in revenue deposit.
Hence, petitioners would not be entitled for any relief in the above writ petition.

5. Insofar as reliance placed on judgment passed in W.P.No.32186/2010, wherein preliminary and final notifications were quashed by order dated 11.07.2014, it was stated that respondent no.2 has preferred Writ Appeal no.1783/2014 wherein order of learned single judge was stayed and appeal was admitted.
Subsequently, present matter is heard and reserved for judgment.
Said status would not lend any benefit to petitioner and sought for dismissal of writ petition.

6. Learned AGA supported submission of respondents no.2 and 3.
7. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused writ petition records.
NC: 2023:KHC:41200 8.
From above submission, it is seen that respondents have vehemently denied assertion of petitioners that respondents have not proceeded with acquisition.
There is specific assertion about passing of award with participation of petitioners and taking possession.
Statement of objections was filed on 12.01.2021.
Until now there is no rejoinder filed denying or contraverting assertions in the same.
At this stage, learned counsel for petitioners submitted that petitioners intend to file representation to BDA seeking benefit under Sections 38(D) of BDA Act.
9. In view of above submission while holding that petitioners would not be entitled for any relief as sought for in this writ petition.
In view of above, writ petition is dismissed, but by reserving liberty to petitioners to avail any other benefit, if entitled to in law.

10. Insofar as W.P.No.10854/2020 also it is seen that acquisition has proceeded with due participation of petitioners leading to passing of award and ending with NC: 2023:KHC:41200 payment of compensation on 17.08.2013 by cheques bearing nos.230557, 230558, 230559 and 230560 of Rs.10 lakhs each, while petitioner opted for portion of developed land, in lieu of compensation.
Thus compensation is received and possession taken by BDA on 09.03.2012 by drawing mahazar signed by petitioner and his brothers.
Since indemnity bond, agreement as well as mahazar has been signed by petitioner also, petitioner would not be entitled for relief as sought for in this writ petition.
Consequently, writ petition is dismissed.
